subject: GPU fleet sculpting + activation tempo proposal — Ember Health

Subject: GPU fleet sculpting + activation tempo proposal — Ember Health

Alex —

Thanks for the time today. Attached is a compact proposal that ties the reservation sizing to the expected production velocity you described (3000 concurrent chat sessions peak, average response length ~140 tokens). I focused on three practical knobs we can use to align price and performance as you ramp:

- Sculpted cluster sizing: start small with a hot lane (8 x A100-equivalent) + cold pool (40 x A100-equivalent) that we can stage on demand.
- Minimum guarantee (min GPUs): a 12-GPU soft floor during trial to preserve latency SLOs for peak fanout.
- Activation tempo (ramp schedule): a measured 10-week activation line with triggers at MRR milestones — each trigger adds 8 GPUs into the hot lane and re-provisions cold pool capacity.

Highlights in the attached PDF: cost per token at each ramp step, estimated 95th-pct latency under steady-state, and fallback policies (model-variant routing to smaller quantized variants during cold-pool cold starts).

Two asks to keep this moving:
1) Internal confirmation from procurement on the proposed billing cadence (monthly vs. quarterly invoicing).
2) A short call this week with your infra team to validate expected peak concurrency and any network egress constraints.

I fielded the technical sizing with Karthik — he flagged a warmup-credit mechanism we can bake in (two weeks of sealed warmup credits across the hot lane to accelerate KV cache build). That would reduce early token cost and spike latency while you reach your steady-state traffic.

Attachments: ember_health_capacity_slate_v1.3.pdf; mutual-action-plan-ember-2028.xlsx

Best,

— David

David / Karthik —

Looping in procurement (see cc). A couple of procurement-minded constraints:

- Ember prefers quarterly invoicing; payments net-45. Is there any flexibility on net-30 for committed reservations?
- We need a firm definition of "min GPUs" in the contract so it isn't interpreted as a hard purchase requirement during early pilot. Can this be a "billing floor" that automatically converts to actual capacity only after we hit the first ramp trigger?

Technical note from our infra lead (attached inlined): we will have bursty ETL jobs that run nightly around 02:00 local time; if the cold pool activation has 20–30s cold-starts we risk throttling the ETL. Any warmup strategy needs to include a scheduled pre-warm for those windows.

Lastly — can you provide an explicit table showing: week-by-week GPU count, estimated token burn, and estimated monthly cost (commit vs. on-demand) for the first 12 weeks? That makes forecasting far easier for my CFO.

I'll sit tight for the updated slate and the call invite.

— Alex
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Russo <alex.russo@emberhealth.ai>, Procurement <procurement@emberhealth.ai>

Subject: Re: GPU fleet sculpting + activation tempo proposal — Ember Health

Great questions — short answers up front, details below.

- Invoicing terms: We can support quarterly invoicing with net-45 for this pilot. For committed reservations we prefer net-30, but for strategic pilots (like yours) we will accept net-45 and a PO.
- Billing floor behavior: We will express the 12-GPU minimum as a "billing floor" in the contract (you are billed for the floor every month), but capacity provisioning is dynamic — we will only instantiate additional physical GPUs when traffic triggers the ramp steps. The floor buys you latency consistency without forcing you to pay for idle hardware beyond the bill.

Per your infra note: the nightly ETL window is precisely the use-case for scheduled pre-warm. Karthik suggests a simple pre-warm cron (02:00 local) that tours the hot lane and spins up the cold pool in a warm state 15 minutes prior to ETL. With warmup credits applied to the first two nightly windows, we estimate ETL latency will stay within your threshold.

Attached: a 12-week break-down table (week, hot-lane GPUs, cold-pool GPUs, estimated token burn, projected cost under committed vs on-demand). Summary below (high level):

Week 1–2: 12 GPU billing floor; actual instantiated: 8 hot + 8 cold (hot prioritized). Warmup credits -> ~40% token-cost reduction vs on-demand in week 1.
Week 3–4: trigger 1 (MRR milestone) -> add 8 GPUs to hot lane (now 16 hot), cold pool trims to 32. Projected ~28% committed unit cost improvement.
Week 5–8: steady ramp with two more triggers; hot lane grows to 32 by week 8; cold pool holds ~24–28 for buffer.
Week 9–12: scale to target steady state (48 hot, 16 cold) or pause depending on traffic.

We will send the explicit week-by-week CSV as part of the mutual action plan; it's included in the updated attachment.

Next steps:
- I'll drop the updated capacity_slate and M-A-P to the DocuSign link for signature and to HubSpot so your CFO can see the cost table.
- Can we meet Thursday 14:00 PT for the infra sync? If that works I'll include a short agenda: peak concurrency validation; ETL pre-warm schedule; and billing-floor clause language.

Thanks — looking forward.

— David

David —

Thanks for the clarifications and the updated slate. Procurement confirms we can accept quarterly invoicing, net-45, subject to a PO and the contract language that defines the 12-GPU "billing floor" as non-provisioning (i.e., billing-only until a ramp trigger is hit). Two small asks for the contract team:

1) A clause that defines "ramp trigger" with objective metrics (e.g., sustained 95th-pct concurrency > X for Y minutes) so there's no ambiguity when additional GPUs are instantiated.
2) A modest early-termination credit if Ember needs to decommit within 90 days due to clinical compliance gating.

If you can add those three items to the M-A-P and push to the DocuSign link, we can get the PO processed the same week. Also — please include the explicit weekly cost CSV for the CFO.
